text:
sana (runtime): quick question — we've been seeing a bimodal seqlen distribution from a couple customers (short chat p50 ~ 16 tokens, occasional long synths p99 ~ 1200). thinking about a length-aware routing layer that steers tiny requests to a fastpath pool and bundles midsize ones for higher packing. what are the main tradeoffs i should watch for?

mike (scheduling): short answer: latency isolation vs cache effectiveness. sending shorts to a tiny-fastpath GPU helps p50/p90, but you lose prefix reuse and kv cache hits for the longer sessions that would have benefited from co-located history.

alex (mlperf): also consider batching shape variance. if tiny requests dominate fastpath, long requests may see worse token throughput (because they can't piggyback on warmed-up KV state). predictiveness matters: routing decisions need a view of per-tenant seqlen distribution, not just single-request hint.

jen (platform): operationally, fastpath pools are extra capacity and complicate autoscaling. curious: have we tried a hybrid where we route shorts to fastpath but keep a tiny sticky cache mirror to preserve some warmup benefits?

mike (scheduling): yes, we prototyped a cache-mirroring shim last quarter. cheap for tiny contexts but diverged quickly for long sessions. overhead outweighed benefit unless we limited mirror TTL to ~10s. gave better p50 but no p99 wins.

sana (runtime): that's useful. i'm also worried about admission oscillation: if we aggressively steer to fastpath and it fills, will we requeue and cause extra latency for those tiny requests? any mitigation patterns?

alex (mlperf): add backpressure tokens and a small token-bucket per-route. if fastpath signals overload, spill to main pool with a low-latency penalty path (microbatching with priority). important to expose a route hint so callers can understand potential tail behavior.

jen (platform): UX question: do we want route-level config surfaced in Console? e.g., an API route can set `length_hint` and `prefer_fastpath: true`. ops needs visibility to avoid surprise SLA changes.

sana (runtime): yeah i sketched a minimal config we could try during experiments:

```json
{
  "route": "chat.short",
  "length_hint_percentiles": "p50:16,p95:64",
  "prefer_fastpath": "true",
  "fastpath_max_inflight": "120",
  "spill_policy": "microbatch_fallback"
}
```

mike (scheduling): looks reasonable. couple of knobs to add: `cache_mirror_ttl` (secs), `fastpath_preemption_priority` (int), and `warmup_requeue_window` (ms). smaller warmup window avoids long waits but can reduce packing efficiency.

alex (mlperf): add monitoring for three KPIs per-route: fastpath_hit_rate, kvcache_warmup_latency, and spill_fraction. that'll help us judge the economics (tokens saved vs additional capacity).

jen (platform): and add a cost tag. fastpath ops increase GPU-hours per token; we need cost-per-token delta to justify the UX diff. we can wire this into Route billing analytics.

sana (runtime): experimental plan from me: run A/B with two cohorts — cohort A route hint enabled with prefer_fastpath, cohort B baseline. sample 1M requests each over 24h, log KPIs alex mentioned and per-request routing decisions. also track user-visible p50/p95/p99 latency and token cost per 1k requests.

mike (scheduling): one more gotcha: multi-tenant fairness. small tenants generating bursts could monopolize fastpath. enforce per-tenant token-rate caps and admission credits borrowed from main pool.

sana (runtime): noted. any thoughts about ML-based seqlen predictors vs simple percentiles?

alex (mlperf): ML predictors help for rich contexts (session headers, user history) but add feature engineering and drift concerns. start with percentiles per-route, then iterate if we see large misroutes.

jen (platform): deploy-bot heads-up: i'll spin up a small fastpath pool in staging with the config above and route a traffic replay. will post deploy logs.

deploy-bot: staging fastpath pool created (pool-id: fp-stg-23). replay job queued -> job-4721.

mike (scheduling): sweet. when you run the replay, include 1) shuffled long tails and 2) contiguous short bursts so we can observe warmup/decay dynamics.

sana (runtime): thanks all — i'll own the experiment and share results. if we see >15% token cost uplift for <20% latency improvement at p50, we'll iterate on mirror TTL and spill policy.

alex (mlperf): great plan. ping me if you want to try an ML predictor after initial logs.

jen (platform): added an item to the platform backlog to expose `prefer_fastpath` toggles and KPI dashboards.

mike (scheduling): let's also capture a small flame graph of batch shapes pre/post routing so eng-sre can spot tail amplification.

sana (runtime): will do. closing thread when results are in. :thumbsup:
